analysis:
All changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md (head text, updated 2026-10-11, App Attest v3 endpoint binding, same-process endpoint resumption, logout token revocation, erasure/APNs runtime state), docs/consumer/verification.md (new paragraph at head lines 64-69 on the provider endpoint-resumption candidate), and docs/developer/build.md (native serving qualification note; Metal asset-catalog download retry capped at three within the existing deadline). No executable code, auth logic, or configuration changed.

Security-relevant claims were checked against TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 (T-052..T-058). The added verification.md text states that the resumption candidate is custody evidence only: it is not a new Apple proof, does not extend proof validity, and creates no consumer-verifiable credential. It also says provider support does not imply a deployed platform counterpart. This matches the existing model (authorization stays coordinator-derived, final-dispatch recheck via authorizeInferenceHandoff). The identity-binding.md text says the private X25519 key stays in memory, is not persisted, and that a new process or stale socket cannot answer for an old endpoint. That is consistent with A-003/T-011.

The build.md retry is bounded and explicitly retains fail-fast behavior for other errors. The qualification entry is described as requiring explicit opt-in and a verified release app.

The docs reference code paths (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift, CoordinatorClient.answerAppAttestResume, protocol-messages.md anchor, provider-logout revocation) that were not supplied. The backend retained-proof and token-revocation implementations cannot be verified from this batch, but the docs mark them as platform-owned and not claimed as deployed. Later passes should check any code PRs implementing the endpoint-resumption protocol and the device/revoke endpoint against these documented invariants, specifically replay and nonce binding and account/revocation checks.
